text:
sam: Heads-up — we saw a production hit when clients sent both X-Cust-Route and a predictive UA header. Looks like gateway picks X-Cust-Route but some downstream quota checks read UA and split traffic. Anyone seen this clash before?
olivia: yeah saw it on staging yesterday. The problem is double-sourced routing metadata. We route by X-Cust-Route if present, else UA inference. But quotas/readers sometimes use inferred tenant from UA.
raj: is the UA inference deterministic? we were using fuzzy rules that map agent substrings -> tenant hints, so not 1:1.
mira: logging shows ~0.6% of requests had both headers and a mismatch in the tenant id. That triggers quota enforcement on the wrong tenant.
sam: So we need a precedence rule and an audit/breakglass UX. Two options: 1) strict precedence: custom header always wins and we reject/metric if UA maps elsewhere; 2) signed header flow where client signs X-Cust-Route and we trust it fully. Thoughts?
olivia: I prefer signed header route long-term. Short-term, strict precedence + telemetry + a console flag to enable/disable UA-based fallback per route would be safest.
raj: signed headers mean key mgmt + rollout friction. Also how do we handle legacy proxies that strip signatures?
mira: we could implement a gradual rollout: start with strict precedence + telemetry for 2 weeks, then opt-in routes for signed headers, then full enforcement. Add telemetry to count mismatch cases and emit a per-route sample set.
sam: agree. Need API gateway changes: a new config field route.header_precedence = ["X-Cust-Route","UA-inferred"] and route.allow_ua_fallback = true|false. Also emit a mismatch counter and sample to the console.
raj: console UX: show a per-route "header mismatch" heatmap and quick link to sample logs + client UA strings. Also allow toggling allow_ua_fallback with a canary (percent rollout).
olivia: quota logic must read the resolved tenant from the runtime routing decision, not from raw headers. That means we need a deterministic resolver function in proto and unit tests.
mira: propose adding a middleware resolver that runs once per request and attaches "X-Resolved-Tenant" to the request context. Quotas, billing, telemetry all read that.
sam: quick pseudo config for gateway:

```
route:
  match: /generate
  header_precedence: ["x-cust-route", "user-agent-hint"]
  allow_ua_fallback: false
  signed_header: false
```

raj: for signed header support we'll need signer service + rotate keys. Track in infra backlog.

mira: rollout plan checklist: 1) implement precedence and resolver middleware, 2) add mismatch telemetry + per-route sample bucket, 3) console UI for toggling fallback + heatmap, 4) integration tests for quotas tied to resolved tenant, 5) canary enablement for few routes/customers.

sam: I'll open a PR for the resolver middleware and add integration tests. Can someone own the console mockups? @olivia?
olivia: I can do a quick mock today. Also will add a docs note explaining signed header tradeoffs.

raj: FYI deploy-bot: canary deploy after code review pls.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: pr/4823 -> canary cluster (eng-platform-canary). ETA 10m :rocket:
sam: thanks. Also add an audit log entry type for "header_routing_mismatch" that includes sample headers (PII scrubbed) so compliance can review.
mira: noted. I'll work with security to define scrub rules.
sam: ok let's sync in the morning if telemetry shows >0.1% mismatches after canary. :thumbsup:
